questions.q: What is Microsoft Purview, per this lesson?
options: A single screen inside the Azure portal for managing storage accounts
A unified product family for data security, data governance, and data compliance, reachable from one portal
A third-party tool unrelated to Microsoft 365 or Azure
A programming language for writing data pipelines
questions.explain: Microsoft Purview is a unified set of solutions for securing, governing, and maintaining compliance over data wherever it lives, organized into three pillars and accessed through one portal.

questions.q: Which of Purview's three solution pillars does this course focus on almost entirely?
options: Data security
Data governance
Data compliance
None — it covers all three equally
questions.explain: This course lives in the data governance pillar, which contains the Data Map and the Unified Catalog — occasionally touching data security (sensitivity labels) because that capability is shared across pillars.

questions.q: What is the key difference between the Data Map and the Unified Catalog?
options: They are two names for the exact same screen
The Data Map is the technical backbone that scans and catalogs real sources; the Unified Catalog is the business-facing layer organizing that metadata into domains, glossary terms, and data products
The Data Map is for compliance reporting; the Unified Catalog is for scanning data sources
The Unified Catalog replaced the Data Map and the Data Map no longer exists
questions.explain: The Data Map connects to, scans, and technically catalogs data sources. The Unified Catalog sits on top of it, making that metadata discoverable to business users through domains, glossary terms, and data products.

questions.q: Why does this course exist separately from the conceptual data governance courses already in this catalog?
options: Because those courses were wrong and need correcting
Because this course re-teaches the same governance theory from scratch
Because the earlier courses teach governance theory independent of any vendor, while this course shows how that theory shows up concretely inside one specific product
There is no difference between this course and the earlier ones
questions.explain: This course assumes you already know governance theory and focuses on concrete product details — real portal screens, menu paths, and button names — inside Microsoft Purview specifically.

questions.q: Per this lesson's roadmap, which chapter covers lineage from tools like Azure Data Factory and Power BI?
options: Chapter 1 · Purview Foundations
Chapter 3 · Classification and Labels
Chapter 5 · Lineage and Insights
Chapter 7 · Purview in Practice
questions.explain: Chapter 5, Lineage and Insights, covers lineage from Azure Data Factory, Synapse, Fabric, and Power BI, plus reporting.
